personality_one_liner: A cinematic, expensive, and dark-themed creator tool that feels like a professional film set in your pocket.

spacing.rule: Generous cinematic spacing for layout, tight utilitarian spacing for camera UI overlays.

do's: Use heavy glass blur for bottom tab bar, sticky headers, floating camera controls, and bottom sheets.
Pair blur with a translucent tinted base (≥75% of surface) underneath to guarantee foreground readability.
Use glass for premium feature cards sitting on top of cinematic imagery.
dont's: Never blur body text regions, form fields, or the entire screen.
Do not use glass if the foreground text is illegible against the background image.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Glass / Luxe DARK theme. The app must feel like a premium, cinematic film production tool (think Arri or RED camera UIs combined with Apple's polish).
DO NOT USE ANY BLUES OR PURPLES. The color palette relies on deep Charcoal (`#0A0B0E`) and a cinematic Ruby/Crimson (`#E0115F`) for recording and primary actions.
For the AI Director Camera screen, prioritize high contrast. Overlays (instructions, arrows, safe areas) must use solid glass or pure white to remain highly legible over live camera feeds.

Whenever text is overlaid on image cards (like the Templates on the Dashboard), you MUST use a vertical linear-gradient scrim (top-to-bottom, transparent to ≥70% surfaceInverse) to guarantee WCAG contrast.
Use `Fraunces` for large display headings to give it a classic cinema poster feel, and `Satoshi` for all UI text, labels, and camera UIs.
Keep empty states visually rich with relevant iconography or abstract blurred graphics behind the text. A flat black screen is unacceptable.
Haptics are crucial for a camera app. Trigger haptics when starting/stopping recording, when the AI guides the user to a correct position, and when a clip finishes rendering.
